question_text: What does the term "elastic limit" refer to in the context of a material’s stress-strain behavior?

options.text:
(1)
The point where the material fractures

(2)
The maximum stress before plastic deformation begins

(3)
The maximum stress beyond which the material does not return to its original shape

(4)
The minimum stress required for permanent deformation

explanation:
The elastic limit is the maximum stress a material can withstand while still returning to its
              original shape upon removal of the load; beyond this, permanent deformation occurs.
subject: Physics
source: ScienceLesson.in — Physics / Mechanical Properties of Solids / Test 1

question_text: Which type of stress leads to a change in length of a body without changing its shape?
explanation:
Longitudinal stress (tensile or compressive) causes a change in length along the direction of
              the applied force without altering the shape of the body.
subject: Physics
source: ScienceLesson.in — Physics / Mechanical Properties of Solids / Test 1

question_text: Which of the following best defines stress in the context of mechanical properties of solids?

options.text:
(3)

(4)
Change in volume per unit force

explanation:

              deforming force, given by Stress=FA.

source: ScienceLesson.in — Physics / Mechanical Properties of Solids / Test 1

question_text: Why are I-shaped beams commonly used in construction for load-bearing applications?

options.text:
(1)
They have a higher shear modulus

(2)
They provide a large load-bearing surface with reduced bending

explanation:
I-shaped beams provide a large load-bearing surface and sufficient depth to reduce bending,
              minimizing buckling while reducing weight compared to solid beams.
subject: Physics
source: ScienceLesson.in — Physics / Mechanical Properties of Solids / Test 9

question_text: Why do engineers prefer materials with a large Young’s modulus for designing columns and beams?
explanation:
Materials with a large Young’s modulus are stiffer, requiring greater force to produce small
              deformations, which ensures better resistance to bending and stretching.
subject: Physics
source: ScienceLesson.in — Physics / Mechanical Properties of Solids / Test 9

question_text: In designing bridges, why is it critical to understand the elastic properties of materials?

options.text:
(1)
To increase the weight of the bridge

(2)
To reduce the cost of materials

explanation:
Understanding elastic properties ensures that materials can withstand various loads (traffic,
              wind, weight) without undergoing permanent deformation, maintaining structural integrity.
subject: Physics
source: ScienceLesson.in — Physics / Mechanical Properties of Solids / Test 9
